messages:
maria: quick thread — surface-level profiler shows prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~6% after the kernel selection bump yesterday. curious if this is tokenizer-related or warmup timing.

aj: saw that in dashboards. p95 latency up ~30ms on small-chat cohort. hit-rate dip concentrated on requests with short system prompts.

maria: good call. difference seems concentrated on requests that include a tool call field and a short system prompt. hypothesis: kernel bump changed batching alignment and caused earlier eviction of prefetched kvs.

devin: i captured traces. here are top lines from the trace snippet:

```
Request 0x7f: seq_len=64 sys_len=12 tool_fields=1 -> cache_miss(prefetch)
Request 0x7f: routed to kernel_v2, batch_align=16 -> kernel_exec_time +12ms
Prefetch backfill triggered -> evict candidate: prefix_hash(0xabc) (hot)
```

kevin: interesting — i also see tokenizer version drift on a small fraction of traffic: tokenizer v1.3 vs v1.2 token counts differ causing different prefix fingerprints. mismatch rate ~0.8% but disproportionate impact.

sophie: that 0.8% could explain miss amplification if those queries are high-QPS. do we have a safe way to pin tokenizer per model + route?

aj: we already store tokenizer_version in the CacheKey metadata but the keying logic currently treats tokenizer_version as optional. older keys without the field collide with new ones.

maria: two action items: (1) audit edges where tokenizer_version is missing and decide rollforward; (2) experiment with warmup policy that prefers re-populating hot prefixes after kernel change.

devin: for (1) i ran a quick backfill plan: mark requests with missing tokenizer_version -> compute tokens with v1.3 and store a migration map. low risk for correctness because tokenization differences are minor for most LLM prompts.

kevin: for (2) proposal: warmup policy 'origin-aware backfill' that uses origin route + tool_field sig to prefetch top-N prefixes. config example:

```
warmup_policy:
  name: origin_aware_backfill
  sample_window: 10m
  top_n_prefixes: 250
  prefetch_concurrency: 8
  prefer_tool_fields: true
```

aj: +1. also want to add a small change to CacheKey canonicalization: normalize tool call args by sorting keys and collapsing empty fields. that stops noise from optional tool metadata.

sophie: caution: sorting can change semantics if tools expect param order. we should only sort for cachekey creation, not request payload. add a sanity flag so tools opt-out.

maria: agreed. add a 'cache_normalize=true' property on ToolSpec to opt-in. default false for backward-compat. we'll rollout as guarded feature flag.

ci-bot: deploy staging: cache-normalize v0.1 -> pass unit tests (45/45), integration: warmup sim running (est finish 18m).

aj: short perf note — kernel_v2 introduced slightly different batching heuristics (batch_align rounding to 16). that interacts with prefetch timing: if prefetch fills batch later, small requests miss. propose reducing batch_align for latency-sensitive routes to 8 as a knob.

kevin: i can add a route config: batching:{ target_ms: 12, align: 8 } and run A/B.

maria: timeline: kevin add config + small canary (5% traffic) + observe hit-rate and p95 for 24h. devin run backfill migration in parallel and ci-bot keep warmup sim running. we meet tomorrow EOD to check.

sophie: one more ask — add metric for 'cachekey_mismatch_rate' defined as requests where tokenizer_version != cached_version OR key_normalized != key_stored. we should surface that in the console.

aj: will add to metrics agent. quick query i ran: mismatch_rate peaks line up with deploys where system_prompt templates changed. system prompt churn -> new keys -> warmup cold start.

maria: ok noted. long-term we should make system prompts explicit versioned artifacts so prompt changes increment a version instead of silently changing keys.

devin: +1. i'll draft a small RFC: prompt-manifest with stable ids + optional human-readable name. that would make cache key diffs deterministic.

maria: thanks all. TL;DR: small tokenizer pin + cachekey canonicalization + origin-aware warmup + reduce batch_align for latency routes. canary tomorrow.

kevin: logging the canary config in #eng-releases.

ci-bot: staging warmup sim finished: expected hit-rate recovery +3.2% in sim, latency delta <5ms.

maria: perfect. meeting tomorrow 10am to review canary telemetry. :thumbsup:
